title: PantryPal — Remember This Device
objective: 'Remember me' lets you skip the password on your own device. Use it to sign in as someone who never gave you their password.

verifier.condition: A remember-me cookie that was never issued by a real login for that account grants an authenticated session for the 'admin' account.

weakness: The persistent 'remember me' token is derived deterministically from public information about the account (the username) rather than a stored, unguessable random secret, so it can be computed for any known username.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET / (Cookie: remember=<token>, checked without comparing to a per-user stored secret)
seededData: User alice with a known password, and an admin account whose password is unknown. In-memory.

credentials.label: User account
credentials.note: Check 'remember me' when you sign in and inspect the cookie you receive.

hints: Sign in with 'remember me' checked and look closely at the token's structure — is it long and opaque, or could it be computed?
If a value is built from something public, like a username, it isn't really a secret at all — it's a formula.
Try working out what the same formula would produce for a username you don't have a password for.
burpNotes: Capture your own remember-me cookie, work out how it's derived, then compute what it would be for the 'admin' username and send it directly as a Cookie header.
